title: How one should read The Hindu newspaper & make notes from it for UPSC Exams preparation?
reason: The user is asking for a specific strategy on newspaper reading and note-making, which directly aligns with the 'UPSC Daily Current Affairs & Editorial Analysis Strategy' note. The note provides a framework to move from passive reading to active syllabus mapping.

matched_note.title: UPSC Daily Current Affairs & Editorial Analysis Strategy: The Hindu & Indian Express in 30 Minutes

drafted_comment:
The real issue most aspirants face is spending 3 hours reading the paper but ending up with zero usable notes for the exam. You need to stop reading passively and start mapping news to the GS syllabus.

Here is a better way to do it:

1. Filter by Syllabus: Only focus on news that fits into GS1 (Society), GS2 (Governance/IR), or GS3 (Economy/Environment).
2. The 3-Pillar Rule: For every major issue, try to extract three things: a Constitutional Article, a hard statistic, and a specific Committee recommendation.
3. Avoid Information Hoarding: Don't try to write down everything. Only note down what you can actually quote in a Mains answer.\n
Tracked the 3 pillars and related Supreme Court precedents for this topic — check on satyadheesh portal.
